_comment: The cross-model bench: labels then probes, one cell per (model, task,
objective). Each cell generates its own labels first, so the cell is
self-contained and idempotent -- generate_labels overwrites, the probe
Qwen3-8B is deliberately NOT in the grid. Its capture dirs predate the
numbers for all three objectives already exist under output/decomp/ from
the decomposition run. Re-running it here would burn compute to reproduce
numbers we have, behind a path alias that would rot.
Re-expanding is safe: cells whose captures are not on disk yet fail and
can be retried once they land; finished cells are skipped.
Cells guard on shard count first: a bench cell that starts while its
capture is still writing will train on partial data and report a
confident wrong number. Ask gpt-oss/gsm8k, which trained on 990/1319.
name: bench_crossmodel
command: n=$(ls {cap}/meta.shard*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | wc -l); if [ "$n" -ne {shards} ]; then echo "capture incomplete: $n/{shards} shards in {cap}" >&2; exit 1; fi; mkdir -p shared/xm && .venv/bin/python scripts/generate_labels.py --capture-dir {cap} --out-file {lab} && .venv/bin/python scripts/run_experiment.py --capture-dir {cap} --labels {lab} --out-dir {out} --method logreg --target {target} --seeds 42 1 2 3 4
